title: 9pz admits past the tracker's width: workers and claims count differently
description:
Regression from 9pz, and the tracker caught it. epic dha died:

    claim e9n: tk command "claim" refused: dispatch width exceeded: wave width 4
    is full: 4 implementer(s) already in flight under dha (80x, aqm, b50, cxk).
    Claiming e9n would make 5.

9pz made the WINDOW count only attempts that still have a live worker, so a settled attempt awaiting collect/integrate/gate/close no longer holds a slot — that is the change that bought ~7 minutes per tick. But tk counts CLAIMS, and a claim lives until the tick CLOSES. 80x, aqm and b50 had settled and were waiting to be finished: no worker, still claimed. So the reconciler admitted a fifth claim and tk refused it.

tk is right. The width is enforced where it cannot be argued with, and the refusal names the four holders. The disagreement is ours: 'in flight' means a live worker to the window and an open claim to the tracker, and 9pz made those two numbers diverge for the first time.

Options, none obviously right:
- The window counts CLAIMS for admission (holders, not live workers). Correct against tk, and gives back most of 9pz's gain whenever finishes queue up.
- The claim is released at collect and re-taken at close. Wrong: a released claim invites another run to take the tick while its work is being integrated.
- tk learns the distinction — a claim that is 'settled, being integrated' is not an implementer in flight. Most honest, and the biggest change: it is a tracker-side concept the tracker currently has no reason to know.
- The width is raised. Not a fix: it makes the two numbers disagree by a larger margin.

Decide what 'in flight' means ONCE, for both sides, and make the other follow. Whatever is chosen, the run must never again ask tk for something tk will refuse — the reconciler should not be able to die on its own tracker's guard.

Note for whoever takes it: the epic cannot proceed past four settled-but-unfinished ticks until this is settled, because the run dies rather than holds.
acceptance_criteria: A run never asks the tracker for a claim its width forbids; 'in flight' has one meaning across the window and the tracker; and a queue of settled-but-unfinished ticks neither stalls admission nor kills the run
